question: Can bounded rotated ROI row caching improve resident fine search without changing its ordered results?
scope: Metal gray8; peak mode1 in both GPU methods; fine mode0 original versus mode1 oversized ROI row cache

formal.order: fresh processes with alternating order per block
formal.clock: algorithm total; excludes decode,session construction,JSON andGT

profiling.method: encoder timestamps plusperlevel GPU work counters, final readback only; separate from formal timing

gates.time: per block <= baseline+max(2ms,10%), compare GPU baseline and hybrid separately
gates.primary_target: atleast10% median endtoend time reduction onboth128/512 vs current GPU baseline
gates.memory: report named Metal buffers, diagnostic retained buffers and static threadgroup bytes separately; do notadd toRSS

design: Only oversized rotated ROIs use <=16 template rows with six halo rows; preserve global sampler coordinates, integer moments, scoremap and controls. Verywide ROI uses original direct sampling. No integer narrowing or overlapstatistic reuse thisround.
retention: Keep original mode0 and experimentmode1; freeze source+fixtures, retain allgates, raw measurements and failed attempts. No default route change.
limits: Sampler call counts derived from observed angles are not hardware memory transactions
